name: Mailboxes
tagline: IMAP and POP3 mailboxes your app reads: put a supplier's invoice in, and the app finds it on its next poll.
point: The mailbox address; any password but "wrong" unless you set one

capabilities.title: Put mail in
capabilities.text: put_mail drops a message as if someone sent it: from, subject, text or HTML, attachments, or a whole raw RFC 822 message.

capabilities.title: Real IMAP commands
capabilities.text: SELECT, FETCH with BODYSTRUCTURE and sections, SEARCH, STORE, COPY, MOVE, EXPUNGE, IDLE and the UID commands.

capabilities.title: POP3 too
capabilities.text: STAT, LIST, UIDL, RETR, TOP and DELE over USER/PASS or AUTH PLAIN, with STLS.

capabilities.title: See what the app did
capabilities.text: Every command the app sent, with its time and without passwords, next to the messages it touched.

capabilities.title: Folders and flags
capabilities.text: INBOX first plus any folder; read and deleted flags show whether the app marked or removed what it read.

capabilities.title: Logins like the real thing
capabilities.text: LOGIN, AUTHENTICATE PLAIN and XOAUTH2 (any token); set a password per mailbox or let any password in.

capabilities.title: Mailbox trouble on cue
capabilities.text: A refused login, a mailbox in use, a connection dropped during FETCH, TLS required or an expired OAuth token.

callouts.title: Where to connect
callouts.text: IMAP on 1143 with STARTTLS, POP3 on 1110 with STLS.

callouts.title: Mailboxes
callouts.text: Each address is a login; the count shows unread messages.

callouts.title: Unread
callouts.text: The dot clears when the app sets \Seen; a PEEK fetch leaves it.

callouts.title: Attachments
callouts.text: XML, PDF or images, as a supplier would attach them.

callouts.title: Put the message
callouts.text: From, subject, text and an attachment; the app finds it on its next poll.

excerpts.title: What the app did, and what to break

callouts.title: Put by you
callouts.text: Messages you or an agent put in, with their UID.

callouts.title: The app's login
callouts.text: Each command is logged; passwords never are.

callouts.title: How it fetched
callouts.text: BODY.PEEK[] leaves the message unread; the log shows which form the app used.

callouts.title: Drop during FETCH
callouts.text: The connection closes mid-fetch: does the app retry without losing the message?

callouts.title: XOAUTH2 token expired
callouts.text: The OAuth login is refused, as when a refresh is due.

provoke.name: Login refused
provoke.what: Every login to the mailbox fails

provoke.name: Drop during fetch
provoke.what: The connection closes during FETCH or RETR

provoke.name: TLS required
provoke.what: Plain logins are refused before STARTTLS or STLS

provoke.name: Wrong password
provoke.what: A login with the wrong password is refused

advantages.title: No shared test mailbox
advantages.text: Nobody else reads or deletes the messages, so a poller test sees exactly what you put in.

advantages.title: Messages in a second
advantages.text: put_mail lands at once; no waiting for a real server to deliver and index.

advantages.title: Watch the conversation
advantages.text: The command log shows whether the app used SEARCH UNSEEN, PEEK or EXPUNGE, which a real server keeps to itself.

advantages.title: Failures servers rarely give
advantages.text: Drops during FETCH, INUSE and expired XOAUTH2 tokens come when you ask, to test retries.

agent.prompt: Check that our invoice importer picks up an XML attached to an e-mail.
steps: Invoice 1234 read; the app ran LOGIN, SELECT INBOX, SEARCH UNSEEN, FETCH 3
